messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
You are dealing with A shared tray of spare parts when it comes back with a minor modification you did not request. You may need the item yourself later. Describe your next move.

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R025", "response": "I tap the tray once with a knuckle, then leave it alone for one second. I mark the worn slot with grease, leave the spare part beside it, and leave the tray alone for another turn. If it starts clicking, I mark again."}, {"id": "R026", "response": "i put the tray down and check the small screw on the rim. if it stays in place, i leave it for a moment. if it goes into the rim, i ask the maker if they have any other screws left."}, {"id": "R027", "response": "i photograph the tray and mark the minor change. then i return it to the machine. sorry—sorry, i’m checking whether i want the spare before i leave the note. i leave the mark and check whether the replacement fits."}, {"id": "R028", "response": "i take the tray and place it on the spare part, then check the original part. i mark the spare part with ‘modified’ and put it in the drawer. i keep the original part in case it needs it."}, {"id": "R029", "response": "I tap the tray once and set it beside the old one. I tap the new slot twice and leave the old one beside the old one. I tap the tray once more."}, {"id": "R030", "response": "I turn the tray once between finger and thumb. The small crack shows where a tooth was missed. I put the plate back on the bench and leave the door open. Tomorrow may have the missing piece, but the change has already been made."}, {"id": "R031", "response": "i tap the tray once with my thumbnail, then i put the spare part back in the same place. i write the name on the corner, then move it to the end. i keep the tray in my pocket, but i do not touch it again."}, {"id": "R032", "response": "I put the tray down and rub the old drawer handle. “I put the spare in the drawer first. Then I try the new part and see if it slips.” I put the drawer back and leave the drawer open for now."}, {"id": "R033", "response": "I tap the tray twice and keep the old part beside it. I tap the old slot with my heel, then leave the new one beside it. I keep the old one closed, though I keep my hand near the old slot. I test the hinge with a folded strip of paper, then leave the old part seated."}, {"id": "R034", "response": "i move the tray slowly and leave the small part behind. i write the note on a scrap and keep the rest."}, {"id": "R035", "response": "I take the spare and test the small bolt. “I put it in the same pocket. Then I take the old one and leave the new one in the tray. That small change may be useful.” I pocket the bolt and the small bolt, but the new one stays in my hand. the tray may be waiting for the next piece."}, {"id": "R036", "response": "i tap the tray with my greasy thumb. “useful,” i say. i leave the spare part on the table. i move the tray closer. “not mine yet.” i pocket the rusted bolt."}]
